note: ONE table for the instrument palette: registry rows AND engine facts. server/daw/instruments.py, store.js and routes.js all read THIS file; a patch added on one side only cannot exist. Samples live OUTSIDE the repo under <appData>/daw/instruments (AIPLAY_DAW_INSTRUMENTS overrides); the downloader in patches.js fetches packs on demand, licence first.

tr808.label: TR-808 machine (13 analogue voices)
tr808.quality: Zero-download, zero-licence, fully tunable. The 808 is entirely analogue, so every voice here is the real topology (bridged-T rings, the six-oscillator metal cluster at 205.3/304.4/369.6/522.7/540/800 Hz, the three-burst clap) — not a sample of one. 90-95% against a commercial 808 sample pack, and better than any of them on control: 15 knobs instead of a folder of frozen wavs. The 808 has no ride cymbal; keys 51/59 answer with a damped cymbal.

kick_decay.doc: Ring damping: 0.04 s to 0.24 s tau (T60 0.28 s to 1.66 s).

kick_drive.doc: Output saturation. 0 is a pure sine, exactly.

kick_click.doc: The TONE transient: a 0.7 ms high-passed pulse from the trigger.

snare_tune.doc: Both shell rings (180 Hz and 330 Hz at 0).

snare_snappy.doc: The front-panel SNAPPY balance: shell against wires.

hat_decay.doc: Closed hat, 8 ms to 38 ms tau.

openhat_decay.doc: Open hat, 30 ms to 250 ms tau.

cymbal_decay.doc: Cymbal, two-stage: 60 ms to 440 ms tau on the fast stage.

clap_decay.doc: The room tail after the three bursts.

tom_tune.doc: All three toms and the congas.

spread.doc: Per-voice stereo placement. 0 is the machine's real mono output.

tr909.label: TR-909 machine (analogue kick/snare/toms + synthesised metals)
tr909.quality: A different circuit from the 808, not a re-tune: triangle-core kick under a deep fast glide with its own noise ATTACK stage, noise-led snare with a TONE high-pass. 85-90% on the kick/snare/toms. HONEST GAP: the real 909's hats, ride, crash, clap and rim were 6-bit PCM samples, not circuits — those five here are synthesised stand-ins (~70%), useful but not the ROM.

kick_sweep.doc: How long the glide from 5.2x down onto the fundamental takes.

kick_attack.doc: The ATTACK stage: click plus a 5 ms noise burst. This is the punch.

kick_drive.doc: Output saturation. 0 is exactly the unsaturated triangle.

snare_tune.doc: Both triangle rings (185 Hz and 330 Hz at 0).

snare_tone.doc: High-pass on the noise, 1.2 kHz to 6 kHz.

hat_decay.doc: Closed hat, 7 ms to 33 ms tau.

openhat_decay.doc: Open hat, 35 ms to 235 ms tau.

clap_decay.doc: The tail after the four bursts.

tom_decay.doc: Tom ring damping, 0.08 s to 0.36 s tau.

tom_noise.doc: The noise blend the 909 toms carry and the 808's do not.

tr808_bass.label: 808 bass (pitched sub, sustains)
tr808_bass.quality: The instrument people mean by "an 808": the 808 kick circuit with the decay opened up and the pitch tracking MIDI. The ONLY machine voice that honours note LENGTH — write a two-bar note and it holds for two bars. Saturation and click are knobs, so it can be a clean sub or a distorted trap lead.

tune.doc: Offset from the played MIDI pitch.

decay.doc: 0.15 s to 6.0 s tau. High values sustain through a whole bar.

release.doc: Fall after note-off, 10 ms to 190 ms tau.

bend.doc: Pitch excess at the strike, as a fraction of the fundamental.

bend_time.doc: How fast that excess settles, 8 ms to 68 ms.

click.doc: High-passed attack transient — what makes it audible on a phone.

drive.doc: Saturation. Adds the harmonics small speakers reconstruct the sub from.

hybrid_kick.label: Hybrid sub kick (clean sub + transient layer)
hybrid_kick.quality: Not a vintage model. A mathematically clean sine sub with a fast pitch snap and a SEPARATE transient layer (beater knock + click) on its own knob — so the attack can be pushed for laptop speakers without touching the low end. The modern pop/trap kick that has to sit under a dense mix.

tune.doc: 48 Hz at GM key 36; the voice key-tracks from there.

decay.doc: Sub decay, 0.05 s to 0.33 s tau.

pitch_amount.doc: How far above the fundamental the glide starts (up to 8x).

punch.doc: The transient LAYER: a 280-1100 Hz beater knock plus a 2.2 kHz click.

drive.doc: Saturation on the sum. 0 keeps the sub a mathematically pure sine.

meatbass_arco.label: Meatbass — arco (bowed)

vsco2_strings_pizz.label: Violin section — pizzicato (VSCO2)
vsco2_strings_pizz.quality: Section pizz with 2 round-robins per note.

vsco2_glock.label: Glockenspiel (VSCO2)
vsco2_glock.quality: Bright and clean; long natural ring.

eguitar_clean.label: Electric guitar — clean (FSBS)
eguitar_clean.quality: 55-60% vs a commercial electric-guitar library. What it has: 29 key zones over E1-D6, 24-bit/48 kHz stereo FLAC, 4 random round robins. What it does not: only 2 velocity layers, so it plays flat under dynamics, and no slides, bends, harmonics or palm mutes. For a driven tone put a saturator insert after it — that is a better answer than a 300 MB distortion pack.

eguitar_jazz.label: Electric guitar — jazz (FSBS)
eguitar_jazz.quality: 55-60% — the same instrument and mapping with a warmer, rolled-off tone. Same two-velocity-layer ceiling.

growlybass.label: Bass guitar — fingered (Growlybass)
growlybass.quality: 65-70% and the strongest free electric bass there is: Squier Jazz Bass recorded DI, 4 velocity layers x 4 round robins. MEASURED range A1-G#5 (MIDI 33-80), in tune to the cent at A2/E3/A3; keys 81-84 are pick scrapes, not notes. TWO honest limits: the bottom five semitones of a 4-string bass (E1-G#1) are NOT sampled, so put those on meatbass_pizz or transpose them up; and on the lowest notes the second harmonic is louder than the fundamental, which is true of every DI bass and is what a bass amp's low shelf exists to fix. No slides or legato, which this engine cannot voice anyway. Roundwounds about six months old, so it is bright: a tilt EQ insert takes it to Motown. NOT SHIPPED from this pack: the 'vicious' staccato mapping. Its own SFZ has pitch_keycenter=0 on the 59-61 zone and the articulation did not key-track under measurement.

epiano_wurlitzer.label: Wurlitzer EP200 electric piano
epiano_wurlitzer.quality: 50-55%. 48 key zones over A1-C7 with 4 velocity layers on most of the range. HONEST GAP: a real Wurlitzer barks when you hit it hard and this sampling is too sparse to bark — push a saturator for that. CC-BY: using it adds a credit line to every render and bounce.

epiano_pianet.label: Hohner Pianet T electric piano
epiano_pianet.quality: ~50%. 49 key zones, 3 velocity layers. The Pianet is a one-dynamic instrument by nature, so the thin layering costs less here than it does on the Wurlitzer. CC-BY: credit line on every render.

epiano_cp80.label: Yamaha CP80 electric grand
epiano_cp80.quality: ~55%. Full 88 keys (A0-C8), 4 velocity layers — the widest-ranged of the three. Real strings through a pickup, so it sits between a piano and an electric piano. CC-BY: credit line on every render.

organ_drawbar.label: Drawbar organ
organ_drawbar.quality: ~45%, and honest about why: this is SAMPLED FROM setBfree, a free tonewheel emulator, at ONE frozen drawbar registration. No drawbar control, no Leslie, no key-click variation. It is a usable organ bed for 7 MB; it is not a Hammond you can play.

organ_percussive.label: Percussive organ
organ_percussive.quality: ~45%. The same setBfree source with the percussion tab engaged — the attack click that makes an organ line articulate. Same frozen-registration limits as the drawbar patch.

organ_rock.label: Rock organ
organ_rock.quality: ~45%. A driven registration, and the only one of the three in real stereo (each key is a hard-panned sample pair). Same frozen-registration limits.

muldjord.label: Muldjord kit (rock/metal, GM-mapped)
muldjord.quality: 70-75% and a genuinely different voicing from the two AVL kits: Tama Superstar, recorded for a metal band, 2 kicks / snare / 4 toms / hats / 2 crashes / 2 rides / china. Deep velocity layering with 4 RANDOM round robins per layer, stereo 24-bit FLAC. The pack's own layout is keys 48-66; this row carries a key_map so a GM beat plays it unchanged. CC-BY: credit line on every render.

harp.label: Concert harp
harp.quality: ~60%. 36 zones over E1-F#7, 3 velocity layers, edited from the VCSL recordings. No glissando articulation and no pedal changes, but a harp played as arpeggios is forgiving and this is 6 MB.

sax.label: Saxophone — generate this part
sax.refusal: Sax is the notoriously weak family in free AND commercial sample libraries (40-50% honest quality, no legato/growl scripting). This patch refuses to fake it: generate the part with Music 3.0 instead — the fork wires generation as a first-class instrument answer.
sax.quality: GAP named on purpose — generation is the honest answer for lead sax.

sitar.label: Sitar — generate this part
sitar.refusal: No quality free-licensed sitar sampleset exists (25-30% is the honest ceiling of a GM program). This patch refuses to fake it: generate the part with Music 3.0 instead.
sitar.quality: GAP named on purpose — generation covers the real use.

choir.label: Choir — generate this part
choir.refusal: Free choir samples are pad-grade ahh/ohh only — no words, no legato (~50%). This patch refuses to fake it: Music 3.0 generates vocal pads and choirs well; that is the first-class answer.

solo_cello.label: Solo cello — generate this part
solo_cello.refusal: Exposed solo strings are the one family money actually buys (45-55% free ceiling: fine under a mix, not exposed). This patch refuses to fake an exposed cello line: generate it with Music 3.0 instead.
solo_cello.quality: GAP named on purpose — the solo-string ceiling is real.

acoustic_guitar.label: Acoustic guitar — generate this part
acoustic_guitar.refusal: Acoustic guitar is the one family where the free ceiling is genuinely too low to ship, and this row exists so the gap has a name instead of a disappointment. Everything licence-clean measured 30-45%: FreePats FSS Steel-String is a subset of an old GigaSampler set AND is GPL-3 on the audio (a different legal posture from every other pack here, needing an owner decision, not an agent's); FreePats Spanish Classical is CC0 but its own page says the recording conditions were far from ideal; the Discord GM Martin HD28 has a single velocity layer. Electric guitar is a different story and IS installed (eguitar_clean / eguitar_jazz). For acoustic: generate the part with Music 3.0, or use GeneralUser GS program 25 for a sketch that is honestly a sketch.
acoustic_guitar.quality: GAP named on purpose — free acoustic guitar tops out at 45% and the best of that is GPL-3 audio. Electric guitar is covered.
